info.name: CYBERBIZ Webhooks
info.description:
CYBERBIZ Webhooks

## Usage

This collection replays every documented CYBERBIZ Event against your own webhook receiver, with the same headers, payloads and signatures CYBERBIZ sends.

1. Create a Postman environment with your receiver's `webhookUrl`, your shop's `shopDomain` / `customDomain` and the real `appSecret`; never commit it.
2. Send a request. The collection's pre-request script computes `X-Cyberbiz-Hmac-Sha256` (HMAC-SHA256 of the exact body bytes) and `X-Cyberbiz-Domain-Hmac-Sha256` (hex HMAC-SHA256 of the base64 of `shopDomain`, as the platform computes it) with `appSecret`; the body signature uses the encoding selected by `signatureEncoding`.
3. The collection's test expects a 200: your receiver should answer quickly and process the Event asynchronously.

Payloads are synthetic Samples generated from the same source as webhooks.md; they contain no variables so the signature always matches the bytes sent.

## Release Notes

### 2.1.0 (2026-10-14)

- webhooks.md and the webhook Postman collection document 38 more events from the source-derived webhook collection, including the four Merchant-webhook job events.

### 2.0.1 (2026-10-14)

- The webhook Domain Signature is documented and computed as the HMAC-SHA256 of the base64-encoded X-Cyberbiz-Domain, which is what the platform signs.

### 2.0.0 (2026-10-09)

- Removed the /v1/limit_collections endpoints: the platform does not serve them on app-store-api.cyberbiz.io.

### 1.1.0 (2026-10-09)

- Product create and POS batch create document the sku request parameter, which the platform requires for shops with the POS feature.

### 1.0.1 (2026-10-02)

- Postman collection descriptions no longer point to repository-internal files.

### 1.0.0 (2026-09-08)

- Initial generation from the CYBERBIZ v1 swagger, the v1/v2 Postman collections, the Notion v2 reference and the webhook reference.
- Observed corrections applied: nullable fields, money as float, order_number as integer, arrays documented as objects, fields missing from the swagger, Bearer authentication.
- Synthetic samples derived from the Golden Files for every operation and event.

variable.description: Your receiver's HTTPS URL. Override it in your own Postman environment (*.postman_environment.json files are never committed).
The Shop Domain sent as X-Cyberbiz-Domain and signed into X-Cyberbiz-Domain-Hmac-Sha256. Override it in your environment.
The merchant's custom storefront hostname sent as X-Cyberbiz-Shop-Domain. Override it in your environment.
The App Secret used to sign the requests. Set the real one in your own Postman environment, never in this collection.
`hex` or `base64`. Production App webhooks send hex (64 characters) although CYBERBIZ's documentation says base64; see ADR-0001. Switch to `base64` to test the documented form.

CYBERBIZ sends `orders/create` when: An order was placed. The body is the `Order` payload object, exactly as documented in webhooks.md; the pre-request script signs it with `appSecret`.

A 401 from your receiver usually means its App Secret differs from `appSecret`.
